text:
meera: Quick callout — observed a non-linear throughput drop on L4 when seq_len > 1024, looks like kernel selector is picking a fallback GEMM at certain windows.

alex: Ugh. Is this on the new autotuner build?

meera: Yes, landed yesterday (autotune v2). A100/H100 unaffected. L4/T4/A10 show 20-40% lower tokens/s for some prompt mixes.

tom: Any flamegraphs / nvprof traces? Last time similar thing was a cache-miss blowup in the KV path.

meera: Attached short profiler excerpt (pasted):
```
# seqlen=128: matmul_fast 75% time, kv_hotpath 10%
# seqlen=1536: matmul_fallback 62% time, kv_eviction_spike 18%, memcpy 12%
# kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_fallback (score=0.42) vs matmul_fast(score=0.39)
```

luis: Interesting that scores are so close. Looks like the scoring function penalizes memory when configured with small workspace for L4. Autotuner may be overfitting to average seqlen=256.

alex: Could also be quantized kernel sensitivity: for int8 paths we use a different tiling that breaks down >1024. Did we change quant cfg in v2?

meera: We changed "workspace_budget_ratio" default from 0.25 to 0.18 to reduce OOMs on A10. Might be unintentionally biasing picks.

tom: Proposed experiments: 1) run kernel-selector dry-run for seqlen sweep [128,256,512,1024,1536,2048] on L4 & A100; 2) force workspace_budget_ratio=0.25 on L4 to compare; 3) enable kv-prefetch heuristic to avoid eviction spikes.

alex: +1. Also add metric: tokens/s and p99 latency for single-stream, and a micro-benchmark that isolates GEMM only.

luis: I'll add a quick patch to make seqlen-weighting explicit in the autotuner (add 0.6*seqlen_factor + 0.4*mem_penalty). That should prefer faster kernel for long sequences.

meera: Thanks. Can someone kick off perf runs? CI bot — if we submit a branch x/autotune-seqlen-weight, can you run L4/T4/A10/A100 matrix for seqlen sweep?

ci-bot: Received: x/autotune-seqlen-weight. Scheduling perf-matrix: devices=[L4,T4,A10,A100], seqlen=[128,256,512,1024,1536,2048], cases=single_stream,multi_stream. ETA ~ 3h. :gear:

tom: If CI shows improvement on L4 but regression on A100, we should make the seqlen_weight an architecture-specific override rather than global change.

alex: Also check batching heuristics — the batcher sometimes expands max_batch when it thinks latency headroom exists, but with large seq it triggers the slow kernel for all subrequests. Maybe add sequence-aware batching: limit batch expansion if avg_seq > 512.

meera: Good call. I'll open a follow-up issue for sequence-aware batching thresholds and link perf results here. Assigning: luis for selector patch, tom for KV-prefetch tweak, alex for batching heuristic. I'll validate results once CI completes.

luis: On it — will push a small change and tag ci-bot.

ci-bot: Perf run started (job 7821). Logs will appear in /perfs/runs/7821.

meera: Thanks everyone. Hoping this is a config/heuristic tweak rather than deep kernel bug. Will update thread after results. :+1:
